title: Sippie Thomas name and the Victor sides she was never paid for
summary: Her records appeared as Sippie Thomas, her maiden name, after her manager changed companies; she recalls the 1929 Victor sides and never being paid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well then, I noticed your first records, or some of your records were Sipple Thomas.

Well, that's my maiden name. See, I'll tell you about that, how that was done. See, I don't know for sure but this is what I believe, my manager and the people had an argument. And he then left and went to the

Colonial people (unintelligible). He left the Okeh and came over to (unintelligible). So when he called me to Richard, (unintelligible). And they had my records, Sippie Thomas. So he made my name Sippie Thomas over there. So while (unintelligible) he said the records, Sippie Wallace and Sippie Thomas was the same people. He said, how'd you have two names? I said, I don't know. Somebody sold me, unbeknownst to myself.
(Recording interruption.)
Now, these Victor labels, Ms. Wallace, that I've got listed as Sippie Thomas --
Yeah.

"Go Down," "Sunshine Blues," that was unissued. "But You're Going to Need My Help," "A Mighty Tight Woman," those were issued by Victor under the name Sippie Thomas. And "Ain't Nobody Home but Me." They cut that but didn't issue it.
"Anybody but Me"?
Yeah.

You know how they -- they put it out but my husband was living during the time and he woke up one day and they put some bluebird singing on the back of there, and my husband stopped that record, "Ain't Nobody Home but Me." He stopped it. He heard singing, he said, "Sip, that's you a record that had some bluebird singing but they got -- (unintelligible)."
So was that you?
That was me.
They called you Sippie Thomas, here on these Victors? Was that you singing on those?
Yeah, that was me. Because Matt told me.
Yeah, with Johnny Dodds, with Kid Ory -- do you remember if Kid Ory was on those?
No, I don't remember.
But you say you never got any money for those?
Not a dime (unintelligible).
Not a dime. How about that. That was February, 1929?
Uh-huh.
How did they get those sides?
I'll be darned if I know.
Did you record those for Victor?
I recorded for Victor, let's see, I had to record for Victor. Mr. Peeler took me over. I don't know how I got over to Victor but I (unintelligible).
Yeah. Well, didn't Victor pay you?
I don't remember receiving no money from Victor. I don't remember receiving one dime from Victor.
